title.narrative: Area-Based Response: ( Sennar/Kasala) - Provision of integrated life-saving health, nutrition, and WASH interventions for conflicted affected population in Sennar/Kasala, Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtIMC has been providing interventions in El Suki and Sinja state through an integrated approach addressing the health, nutrition and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs of conflict-affected communities since September 2023 through this project. Since initiating this project in September 2023, it has supported 5 primary health care facilities. Through these health facilities, at least 16, 000 beneficiaries were provided with OPD consultations, supported the referral of 43 patients requiring higher level of care, vaccinated 1,150 children and supported the training of 20 service providers. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTreatment for 114 SAM and 525 MAM cases was provided, while 5,065 people were screened for malnutrition. 2405 beneficiaries underwent IYCF counselling after 10 service providers were trained on nutrition program implementation. Similarly, 1,000 hygiene kits were distributed at HH level, while 1 health facility’s WASH amenities was rehabilitated. Four water quality testing and monitoring conducted. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtWith the onset of the Rapid Support Response incursions into Sinja and the greater areas of Sennar state, the implementation of this project was disrupted. The operating environment became insecure and unsafe for civilians. The program locations including the supported health facilities were rendered inaccessible. Communities were displaced and staff relocated to relatively safer areas. ltbrgtIMC have conducted a rapid needs assessment in Kassala in coordination with the Ministry of Health, while consulting with different partners that were already present in Kassala. The assessment was done in 7 static health facilities and 3 locations identified as IDP gathering sites. he capacity of the health facilities assessed cannot address the increased needs of the host as well as the displaced populations. Essential medicines are unavailable, assisted deliveries are not offered while nutrition services are available in 5 out of the 7 health facilities. There is no IYCF counselling services. Among the 3 locations identified as IDPS gathering sites, there is no access to nearby health facilities. The nearest gathering site is at least 10 kilometers away from Kassala city, while the farthest gathering site is 45 kilometers away, which takes at least 1 hour to travel to get to the nearest facility in Kassala.ltbrgt ltbrgtTo ensure that the displaced communities from Sennar that have sought refuge in Kassala will be provided with access to an integrated package of health, nutrition and WASH services, IMC, therefore proposes to include Kassala within the geographical scope of this project. The proposed intervention will focus on life-saving activities that will enable displaced communities to utilize services from existing health and nutrition service provides as well as expand the services offered to the target host and IDP populations. Aside from supporting these health facilities, International Medical Corps proposes to deploy 1 mobile health and nutrition team to cover the IDP location which is most vulnerable for disease outbreak and malnutrition if needs are not addressed sufficiently. The project will support 5 health facilities which will be chosen according to patient case load, capacity to expand services with the presence of partner support, availability of service providers and access to the facility among host and IDP populations. To ensure that the mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of the displaced communities is addressed, International Medical Corps proposes to train and capacitate healthcare workers, volunteers and other key community stakeholders on Psychological First Aid. Psychological First Aid training will enhance the skills and knowledge of frontline responders on how to respond to people suffering significant distress, provide them with guidance on how to be supportive, do no harm, communicate effectively and connect people to needed services in an emergency. ltbrgtlt/pgt
